Future Russian President Boris Yeltsin stares in amazement at the goods available at an American supermarket. Houston. 1989

In 1989 Boris Yeltsin, at the time a Soviet Parliament and High Council member, visited United States on an unofficial visit. On the way to a scheduled vist to the Johnson Space Center Yeltsin asked to visit a grocery store they were driving past. Yeltsin was shocked by the diversity in the store and when the manager told him they had 30,000 different things for sale Yeltsin first thought that his interpreter misheard.

For comparison, here is what a Soviet grocery store looked like c. 1990.

Source.
